doc.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023

title: Reading the Charlie Brown theme for a 'TV Tunes' session with Will Lee
summary: Will Lee got him a session where he had to read the Charlie Brown theme, so he asked for five minutes with the chart.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I don’t know the reaction of that but it reminds me of something a great story. I don’t know if you’ve done Will Lee yet for your series.

Our long-time, as you know, long bassist on Letterman from start to finish but even before that you know he was a top studio guy. And during — there was a period of time I guess in the ‘90s where some records came out called “TV Tunes,” versions of the great TV themes and stuff that you could buy on a vinyl record. This was in the days of vinyl, and you could get whether it was the Flintstones theme or the different themes to classic shows. And when they could afford it I think they used the originals but otherwise they would cut their own. And Will got me a date one time, after the show, “Paul, can you come and do a session after the show at 7 PM for this guy” you know. I said yes. And I’m there and they said, “We’re doing the Charlie Brown theme,” here it is, for the TV Tunes. And oh my God they’ve written it out, and I’m just — they expect me to read it. Luckily
I knew it a little bit, but I just, and nobody would get this kind of treatment in the studio but I was on television and a little bit I could ask. I just said to the guy [inaudible]
Paul could you say that again because we had a little kerfuffle with our connection.

They said we’re doing the Charlie Brown theme and put out the music and I said, you know, taking advantage that I was a little known from Letterman, I said, “Can you just give me five minutes with the chart myself?” And it was an unusual request but he said, “Yeah sure, guys, take a five.” And I just went to work with my pencil writing in the ledger lines and whatever I had to do [scats] and just figuring out the independence that you need [scats]. You’ve got to keep that going. Then you’re in A flat. But under pressure, you know, I was able. So if you hear it, if you go like on YouTube I think, that’s me playing that, me and Will, me under duress.
